_about: Icebreakers. groupMin/groupMax = how many campers it works for. sayIt = the English everyone must say out loud, per level.

icebreakers.name: Two Truths and a Lie
steps: Each person thinks of three facts about themselves. Two are true, one is a lie.
One by one, say your three facts out loud.
The group votes on which one is the lie.
Reveal the answer. Guessers who got it right earn a point.

middle: I think number ___ is the lie.
confident: Once, I ___.
I'm pretty sure that's the lie because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Beginners can hold up three picture cards instead of writing.

icebreakers.name: Picture Scavenger Hunt
materials: Picture list (no words) for each team
Phones or paper to check items off
steps: Give each team a list made only of pictures: a red thing, something round, a leaf, etc.
Teams find each item in the room or outside.
To check off an item, the team must say its name in English.
First team to finish (with every word said out loud) wins.

middle: We found a ___ next to the ___.
confident: We found a ___. It was hard because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Confident speakers can describe where they found each item.

icebreakers.name: Name and Move
steps: Stand in a circle.
Say your name and one thing you like, with a move that shows it.
The whole group repeats your name, your sentence and your move.
Go around until everyone has had a turn. Then try to say everyone's names.

middle: I'm ___ and I love ___ because it's fun.
confident: I'm ___. On weekends I usually ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Great first-day activity: no reading needed at all.

icebreakers.name: Would You Rather
materials: Two signs: one for each side of the room
steps: Read a question with two choices, like 'pizza or rice?'
Everyone walks to the side of the room for their choice.
A few people from each side say why out loud.
Anyone can switch sides if they hear a good reason.

confident: I'd pick ___, but I understand why people like ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: For beginners, show the two choices as pictures.

icebreakers.name: Find Someone Who
materials: Bingo cards with 'Find someone who…' boxes
steps: Each person gets a bingo card: 'Find someone who plays soccer', 'speaks three languages'…
Walk around and ask questions out loud.
When someone says yes, they sign that box.
First to get a full line shouts 'Bingo!' and reads the names.

confident: Have you ever ___?
Tell me more about that.

icebreakers.levelTip: Use picture boxes for a beginner version.

icebreakers.name: Paper Snowball Fight
materials: One sheet of paper per person
steps: Everyone writes an answer to a fun question, like 'My favorite food is…'.
Crumple the paper into a snowball.
Snowball fight for 30 seconds!
Pick up a snowball, read it out loud, and guess who wrote it.

middle: This says ___. I think ___ wrote it.
confident: I'm guessing ___ wrote this because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Keep the question simple and the snowball fight short.

icebreakers.name: Where I'm From Line
materials: A big world map, or tape on the floor as a map
steps: Lay out a world map or a tape map on the floor.
Everyone stands on a place that matters to them.
Each person says one sentence about that place.
Others can ask one question.

middle: I'm from ___. The food there is ___.
confident: I grew up in ___. Something I miss is ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Let students choose any place: home, a city they love, a dream trip.

icebreakers.name: Name That Song
materials: Short clips of songs the students choose (check them first)
steps: Before camp, ask students for one song they love from home or from now.
Play 10 seconds of a song.
Teams guess who picked it and say one word about how it sounds.
The person who picked it tells the group about it.

middle: This song sounds ___. I think ___ picked it.
confident: This song reminds me of ___ because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Use their world: songs from home and current hits both count.

icebreakers.name: Draw It, Say It
steps: One player from each team picks a word card.
They draw it without letters or numbers.
Their team shouts guesses in English.
The first team to say the exact word gets the point.

confident: It could be a ___, or maybe a ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Pull word cards from today's topic to warm up the key words.

icebreakers.name: Human Knot with Directions
steps: Stand in a tight circle and grab two different hands across the circle.
Untangle the knot without letting go.
The only rule: you must give directions in English.
Time each team. Try again and beat your time.

confident: If you go under there, we can turn around.

icebreakers.levelTip: Good warm-up before the Riding the bus activity (left, right, stop).

icebreakers.name: Word Freeze Dance
steps: Play music. Everyone dances.
Stop the music and hold up a picture card.
Everyone freezes. The first person to say the word out loud gets a point.
Winners pick the next song.

middle: That's a ___. You use it to ___.
confident: It's a ___. I use one when I ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Pull the picture cards from today's topic to warm up the key words.

icebreakers.name: Four Corners Vote
materials: Four picture signs, one per corner
steps: Put a picture in each corner: pizza, rice, tacos, soup.
Ask a question: 'Which one for dinner?'
Everyone walks to a corner.
One person in each corner tells the room why. Then ask a new question.

confident: I'd choose ___, mostly because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Change the pictures every round: sports, places, animals, seasons.

icebreakers.name: Silent Birthday Line
steps: Everyone lines up in order of birthday, January to December.
No talking! Use fingers and gestures only.
When the line is done, go down the line. Each person says their birthday out loud.
Fix any mistakes together.

confident: I was born on ___. We usually celebrate by ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Great for practicing months and ordinal numbers (first, second, third).

icebreakers.name: Simon Says Remix
steps: Play Simon Says with body parts and directions.
After two rounds, a student becomes Simon.
Simon must give every command in English.
Anyone who moves without 'Simon says' becomes the next Simon.

middle: Simon says turn left and jump.
confident: Simon says walk backwards, then touch your right elbow.

icebreakers.levelTip: Beginners can point at the body part as they say it.

icebreakers.name: Musical Question Chairs
steps: Play musical chairs.
When the music stops, the person without a chair picks a question card.
They answer out loud, then stay in the game.
Remove a chair every two rounds.

confident: Honestly, I think ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Nobody is out: answering a question is the 'penalty'.

icebreakers.name: Rock Paper Scissors Fan Club
steps: Everyone finds a partner and plays rock paper scissors.
The loser becomes the winner's fan and follows them, cheering their name.
Winners find new winners. Fans keep cheering.
At the end, two giant fan clubs cheer for the final match.

middle: Let's go, ___! You can do it!
confident: Come on, ___, you've got this!

icebreakers.levelTip: Loud and silly in the best way. Good after lunch.

icebreakers.name: Color Hunt Relay
steps: Split into teams.
Call out a color: 'Something blue!'
Teams run and touch something that color.
The first team to name the object in English gets the point.

confident: We found a dark blue water bottle next to the door.

icebreakers.levelTip: Add shapes later: 'Something round and red!'

icebreakers.name: Mirror Me
steps: Partners face each other.
One person moves slowly. The other copies like a mirror.
Then the leader says each move out loud while doing it.
Switch roles.

middle: Raise your left arm. Turn around.
confident: Slowly lift your right knee while you wave.

icebreakers.levelTip: Practice left and right before the Riding the bus activity.

icebreakers.name: Stand Up If…
steps: Everyone sits.
Say: 'Stand up if you have a brother.'
Everyone who stands says one sentence about it.
Students take turns calling the next 'Stand up if…'

middle: I have two brothers. They are older.
confident: I have a brother who lives in ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Keep it light: pets, foods, games, sports, music.

icebreakers.name: Weather Report Moves
steps: Teach a move for each weather word: rain (wiggle fingers), wind (sway), snow (shiver), sun (stretch).
Call the weather. Everyone acts it out.
Speed up!
Students take turns being the weather reporter.

confident: Tomorrow will be rainy in the morning.

icebreakers.levelTip: Quick energizer for the start of a session.

icebreakers.name: Make a Group Of…
steps: Everyone walks around the room.
Call: 'Make groups of 3 with the same favorite color!'
Students ask each other to find their group.
Each group says what they have in common.

confident: We all like ___, so we're a group.

icebreakers.levelTip: Try favorite season, number of siblings, or favorite fruit.

icebreakers.name: Ball Toss Memory
steps: Stand in a circle.
Toss the ball and say your name and one thing you like.
The catcher repeats what the last person said, then adds their own.
How long can the chain go?

confident: ___ said she loves ___. As for me, ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Practice he/she/they while remembering names.

icebreakers.name: Opposites Run
materials: Word or picture cards spread on the floor
steps: Spread opposite cards on the floor: hot, cold, big, small, fast, slow.
Call a word: 'Hot!'
Teams race to grab its opposite.
They must say both words in a sentence to keep the card.

middle: The soup is hot. The ice is cold.
confident: It's hot outside, but the water is freezing cold.

icebreakers.levelTip: Picture cards make it work for true beginners.

icebreakers.name: Shake Down 5-4-3-2-1
steps: Shake your right hand and count down from 5 out loud.
Then left hand, right foot, left foot.
Then 4, 3, 2, 1 for each.
Repeat in each home language in the room!

confident: Now let's do it in ___!

icebreakers.levelTip: Let students lead the countdown in their own languages.

icebreakers.name: Walk, Talk, Swap
steps: Everyone gets a question card and walks around.
Find a partner. Ask your question, answer theirs.
Swap cards and find a new partner.
After 5 swaps, share the best answer you heard.

middle: What do you do on weekends?
confident: What's something you'd love to learn?

icebreakers.levelTip: Write easier questions on one side and harder on the other.

icebreakers.name: Hot Seat: The Best
steps: One person sits in the hot seat.
The group asks 'What's the best ___?' questions: food, song, place, game.
The person answers fast, with one reason.
Rotate after 3 questions.

confident: Hands down, the best ___ is ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Students learn 'best', 'better' and 'good' without a grammar lesson.

icebreakers.name: Face Card Feelings
materials: Cards with drawn faces: happy, tired, excited, nervous, bored, proud
steps: Spread the face cards in the middle.
Each person picks the face that matches how they feel today.
They hold it up and say the feeling.
Middle and confident speakers add why.

confident: Today I'm a bit ___, mostly because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: A gentle way to check in with students who are having a hard week.

icebreakers.name: Island Three
steps: You're going to an island for a month. You can bring only three things.
Each person picks their three.
Share them with the group.
Vote: whose list would survive best?

confident: I'd take ___, since without it I couldn't ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Beginners can pick from picture cards.

icebreakers.name: Snack Debate
steps: Show two snacks: chips or fruit? Mango or apple?
Split the room by choice.
Each side gets one minute to give reasons.
Anyone convinced can switch sides.

confident: I see your point, but ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Teaches polite disagreeing: 'I see your point, but…'

icebreakers.name: Speed Chat
steps: Make two lines facing each other.
Show a question. Partners talk for 60 seconds.
One line moves one step to the left.
New partner, new question.

confident: If you could ___, what would you do?

icebreakers.levelTip: Students meet everyone in 15 minutes.

icebreakers.name: The Story of My Name
steps: Think about your name. Who chose it? What does it mean?
Share in small groups.
Each group picks one name story to tell everyone.
Practice saying each name correctly.

middle: My ___ chose my name. It means ___.
confident: I was named after ___, because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Shows students their names matter. Ask how to say each name correctly.

icebreakers.name: Pass the Story
steps: Start a story: 'One day, a cat got on the bus…'
Pass the object. The next person adds one sentence.
Keep going around the circle.
The last person must end the story.

confident: Just when everything seemed fine, ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Teach story words: first, then, suddenly, finally.

icebreakers.name: Meet My Partner
steps: Pair up. Ask your partner three questions.
Remember the answers.
Introduce your partner to the group.
The partner says 'Yes!' or fixes anything wrong.

middle: This is ___. He's from ___ and he loves ___.
confident: I'd like you to meet ___, who ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Talking about someone else feels less scary than talking about yourself.

icebreakers.name: If I Were an Animal
steps: Everyone thinks: if I were an animal, which one?
Act it out for 3 seconds.
Say the animal and why.
The group guesses before you say it.

confident: I'd be a ___, since I'm ___ like them.

icebreakers.levelTip: Good for describing words: fast, quiet, strong, funny.

icebreakers.name: High, Low, Wow
steps: Each person shares three things from their week:
High: something good. Low: something hard. Wow: something surprising.
Others can say 'Me too!' or ask one question.
Counselor goes first.

middle: My low was ___. My wow was ___.
confident: The best part of my week was ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Students can skip the 'low' if they prefer.

icebreakers.name: Pocket Show and Tell
steps: Everyone finds one thing in their pocket or bag.
Hide it behind your back.
Give the group one clue. They guess.
Show it and say one sentence about it.

middle: I use this every day to ___.
confident: This means a lot to me because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Phones count, and lead to great conversations.

icebreakers.name: Menu From Home
steps: Everyone draws a dish from home.
Write or say three ingredients.
Present it like a restaurant special.
The group votes on what they want to try.

middle: This is ___. We eat it on ___.
confident: My family makes ___ for special days. It tastes ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Food from home is a favorite topic. Expect lots of energy.

icebreakers.name: Agree or Disagree Line
steps: Read a fun statement: 'Breakfast is the best meal.'
Agree: step left. Disagree: step right. Not sure: stay on the line.
A few people explain their choice.
Students write the next statement.

confident: I partly agree, but ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Keep statements fun and safe: food, sports, music, school.

icebreakers.name: Three Things in Common
steps: Make groups of three or four.
Find three things everyone in the group has in common.
No easy ones like 'we have hair'!
Each group shares their list.

confident: Surprisingly, none of us ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Great for mixing students who don't know each other.

icebreakers.name: Dream Saturday
materials: Paper with morning, afternoon, night boxes
steps: Plan your perfect Saturday. No limits!
Draw or write morning, afternoon and night.
Share it with a partner.
Partners tell the group the best part of each other's day.

middle: In the afternoon, I'm going to ___.
confident: I'd start the day by ___, then ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Practices time words and future tense.

icebreakers.name: Mystery Bag
materials: Everyday objects: spoon, key, ball, comb
steps: Put an object in the bag. No peeking!
One person feels it and describes it out loud.
The group guesses what it is.
Pull it out. Everyone says the word together.

confident: It's cold, metal, and has a hole at one end.

icebreakers.levelTip: Teaches describing words: soft, hard, round, heavy.

icebreakers.name: Who Am I? Sticky Notes
materials: Sticky notes with animals, foods or jobs
steps: Stick a note on each person's forehead without them seeing it.
Walk around and ask yes/no questions.
Others can only answer yes or no.
Guess your word to win. Help others after.

middle: Can I fly? Do I live in water?
confident: Would people find me in a kitchen?

icebreakers.levelTip: Use words from today's topic for practice.

icebreakers.name: 20 Questions: Zoo Edition
steps: One person thinks of an animal.
The group asks yes/no questions. Count them out loud.
Guess in 20 or fewer to win.
The winner picks the next animal.

confident: Is it bigger than a dog but smaller than a horse?

icebreakers.levelTip: Keep a tally on the board so everyone hears the numbers.

icebreakers.name: Sound Detective
materials: Phone or speaker with everyday sounds
steps: Everyone closes their eyes.
Play a sound: a door, rain, a bus, a phone ringing.
Teams whisper, then say their guess.
Points for the right word in English.

confident: It sounds like someone ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Pick sounds from places students go: bus, school, kitchen.

icebreakers.name: Shadow Pose
materials: A sheet and a lamp, or a wall and a phone flashlight
steps: One person stands behind the sheet with a light behind them.
They make a pose: a basketball shot, cooking, a superhero.
The group guesses the action out loud.
Correct guesser goes next.

confident: You look like you're waiting for the bus.

icebreakers.levelTip: Shadows make shy students feel less watched.

icebreakers.name: Secret Fact Match
steps: Everyone writes a surprising fact about themselves. No names!
Mix the papers in a bowl.
Read one out loud. The group guesses who wrote it.
The writer reveals themselves and adds one detail.

confident: It must be ___, they told me once that ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Check papers quickly before reading out loud.

icebreakers.name: Everyday Charades
materials: Action cards: brushing teeth, catching a bus, cooking rice
steps: A player picks an action card and acts it out.
No words, no sounds.
Their team guesses using the full sentence.
Score a point for the right verb.

confident: You're running to catch the bus, but you missed it.

icebreakers.levelTip: Builds everyday verbs students need at home and school.

icebreakers.name: Zoomed-In Photo
materials: Very close-up photos of everyday things (take them yourself)
steps: Show a super close-up photo.
Teams guess what it is.
Zoom out a little each round.
Fewer zooms = more points.

confident: It could be the edge of a ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Photograph things around camp: a shoe, a pencil, a leaf.

icebreakers.name: Hum That Tune
steps: One person hums a song they love. No words!
The group guesses the song or the singer.
The hummer says one thing about the song.
Songs from home count. Teach the group the title.

middle: I know this song! It's by ___.
confident: This song reminds me of ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Everyone's world shows up: hits from now and songs from home.

icebreakers.name: Odd One Out
materials: Sets of four pictures, one doesn't belong
steps: Show four pictures: apple, banana, bus, grape.
Teams decide which doesn't belong.
They must explain why.
Any good reason gets a point, even an unexpected one!

confident: Actually, the banana is the odd one, since ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Reward creative answers. There can be more than one right reason.

icebreakers.name: What Does It Cost?
materials: Pictures of everyday items with real prices hidden
steps: Show an item: a bus pass, a gallon of milk, sneakers.
Teams write their price guess.
Each team says their number out loud.
Closest without going over wins.

middle: We think it costs about ___ dollars.
confident: Probably around ___, depending on the store.

icebreakers.levelTip: Practices numbers and money before the bank activity.

icebreakers.name: What's Missing?
steps: Show the tray for 30 seconds. Everyone says the objects together.
Cover it with the towel. Remove one object.
Uncover. What's missing?
Add more objects each round.

confident: Someone took the ___ that was next to the ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Memory plus vocabulary in one game.

icebreakers.name: Last Letter Chain
steps: Pick a category: food, animals, places.
The first person says a word: 'apple'.
The next word must start with the last letter: 'egg'.
Can't think of one? Ask the group for help.

confident: Let me think… ___!

icebreakers.levelTip: Write the chain on the board so everyone sees the spelling.

icebreakers.name: Don't Say It!
materials: Word cards, each with one 'banned' word
steps: A player draws a card: 'pizza' (banned word: 'cheese').
Describe the word without saying it or the banned word.
The team guesses.
One minute per player.

confident: People usually order it for parties.

icebreakers.levelTip: Pushes students to find new ways to say things.

icebreakers.name: Picture Word Math
steps: Show two pictures: sun + flower.
Teams combine them into one word.
First team to say 'sunflower' wins the point.
Teams then make their own puzzles.

confident: If you put ___ and ___ together, you get ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Try: foot+ball, rain+bow, home+work, bed+room.

icebreakers.name: Blind Portraits
steps: Partners face each other.
Draw your partner without looking at your paper!
Show the (very funny) drawings.
Describe one feature you tried to draw.

middle: I tried to draw your eyes and hair.
confident: It doesn't look like you at all, but I tried to show your smile.

icebreakers.levelTip: Bad drawings are the point. Everyone laughs together.

icebreakers.name: Three-Panel Me
steps: Draw three panels: where you're from, what you love, what you want to do.
Add one word or sentence under each.
Share with a small group.
Hang them on the wall as a gallery.

middle: In the future, I want to ___.
confident: One day I hope to ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Students who can't say much yet can draw a lot.

icebreakers.name: Symbol Name Tags
steps: Write your name in big letters.
Draw three small symbols for things you love.
Wear it!
Walk around and ask about other people's symbols.

beginner: This is soccer. I love soccer.
confident: I drew a ___ because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Day-one favorite: name tags become conversation starters.

icebreakers.name: Fold-Over Monster
steps: Person 1 draws a head and folds the paper to hide it.
Person 2 draws a body without seeing the head. Fold.
Person 3 draws legs.
Unfold! Name the monster and describe it.

confident: This creature lives in ___ and eats ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Great for body parts, numbers and colors.

icebreakers.name: Map My Morning
steps: Draw a map from your bed to camp or school.
Add landmarks: kitchen, bus stop, store.
Walk a partner through your map.
Partner retells your route.

middle: First I go to the kitchen. Then I take the bus.
confident: After breakfast, I walk two blocks to the bus stop.

icebreakers.levelTip: Perfect warm-up for Riding the bus.

icebreakers.name: Group Playlist
steps: Each person adds one song to the group playlist.
Say the song and one word for how it feels.
Vote on the best song for camp mornings.
Play a few seconds of the winners (check lyrics first).

confident: This song always puts me in a ___ mood.

icebreakers.levelTip: Use their world: music connects everyone.

icebreakers.name: English-Only Tower
steps: Teams build the tallest paper tower in 8 minutes.
Rule: only English while building!
Speaking another language = remove one piece of tape.
Measure and celebrate.

confident: If we fold it like this, it might be stronger.

icebreakers.levelTip: Post useful words on the wall: hold, tape, fold, higher, careful.

icebreakers.name: Postcard Home
steps: Draw a camp scene on one side.
On the other, write a short message to someone.
Read it to a partner.
Take it home or hang it up.

confident: You won't believe what happened today: ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Students can write to family, a friend, or their future self.

icebreakers.name: Name Power Words
steps: Write your name down the side of the paper.
For each letter, write a positive word that starts with it.
Decorate!
Share your favorite word and why it fits you.

confident: I picked ___ because it describes how I ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Help with a word list for tricky letters.

icebreakers.name: Design a Sneaker
steps: Design your dream sneaker.
Give it a name and a price.
Pitch it to the group in 30 seconds.
The group 'buys' their favorite with pretend money.

beginner: My shoe is red. It costs ___.
confident: What makes these special is ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Fun for the sneakers & style crowd. Works with any theme.

icebreakers.name: Recipe Card Swap
steps: Draw a dish you know how to make, or want to.
List three ingredients and one step.
Swap with a partner. Read their recipe out loud.
Would you try it? Say why.

confident: The secret is to ___ before you ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Practices kitchen verbs: cut, boil, mix, fry.

icebreakers.name: Caption It
materials: Funny photos you took at camp (with permission)
steps: Show a funny photo with no caption.
Teams write the best caption.
Read them out loud.
The photo's 'star' picks the winner.

confident: Me trying to ___ on a Monday.

icebreakers.levelTip: Use your own camp photos. Ask before showing anyone's picture.

icebreakers.name: Flag of Me
steps: Design a flag that shows who you are.
Use colors and symbols that mean something to you.
Explain one color and one symbol.
Hang the flags together like a camp parade.

confident: The ___ represents my ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Students can include their home country, family, hobbies or dreams.

icebreakers.name: Dough Sculpt Guess
steps: Pick a word card. Don't show anyone!
Sculpt it in 90 seconds.
The group guesses.
Sculptor says the word and spells it.

middle: Is it a kind of food?
confident: It looks like a ___, but maybe it's a ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Hands-on and calm, but still lots of talking.

icebreakers.name: Make Our Camp Chant
steps: Teams make a short chant or cheer for camp.
Use at least three English words and one word from a home language.
Add claps or stomps.
Perform! Everyone learns the winning chant.

confident: Nobody ___ like we ___!

icebreakers.levelTip: Mixing languages in the chant makes everyone feel included.

icebreakers.name: Cup Tower Coach
steps: In each team, one person is the Coach. Coaches can talk but can't touch.
Builders can touch but can't talk.
The Coach looks at a picture of a cup tower and gives directions.
Matching tower wins. Rotate the Coach.

middle: Put the cup on top. Turn it over.
confident: Move the third cup a little to the right.

icebreakers.levelTip: Builds direction words fast: on, under, next to, upside down.

icebreakers.name: Alphabet Room Race
steps: Teams get a sheet with A to Z.
Find something in the room for each letter.
Write it and say it out loud to the counselor.
Most letters in 10 minutes wins.

confident: Is there anything in here that starts with Q?

icebreakers.levelTip: Allow outside the room if it's safe.

icebreakers.name: Category Blitz
steps: Call a category: fruits, jobs, things in a kitchen.
Teams list as many as they can in 60 seconds.
Read lists out loud.
Points only for words no other team has!

confident: Does ___ count as a ___?

icebreakers.levelTip: Unique words score, so students dig for new vocabulary.

icebreakers.name: Human Sentence
steps: Give each person a word card.
Teams line up so their words make a sentence.
Read the sentence out loud, one word per person.
Mix the cards and make a new sentence.

confident: Could / you / tell / me / where / the / bus / stops?

icebreakers.levelTip: Use sentences from today's activity phrases.

icebreakers.name: Balloon Keep-Up Words
steps: Teams stand in a circle with a balloon.
Pick a category: colors.
Each time someone hits the balloon, they say a word from the category.
Balloon touches the floor or a word repeats? Start over and count again.

confident: Doctor! Mechanic! Engineer!

icebreakers.levelTip: Pure fun and loud. Count hits out loud as a team.

icebreakers.name: Drawing Relay
steps: One player from each team runs up and sees the word.
They run back and draw it for their team.
The team shouts guesses in English.
Right answer? The next player runs.

confident: It's something you find at a ___!

icebreakers.levelTip: Use words from the topic you're teaching next.

icebreakers.name: Spelling Relay
steps: Say a word out loud.
The first player runs and writes the first letter.
Next player writes the next letter.
First team to finish the word correctly scores.

confident: Is it double L or one L?

icebreakers.levelTip: Say the letters out loud while writing.

icebreakers.name: Back-to-Back Drawing
steps: Partners sit back to back.
One gets a simple picture (a house, a sun, a tree).
They describe it. The other draws it without seeing.
Compare! Then switch.

beginner: Draw a circle. Draw a line.
middle: Draw a big square in the middle.
confident: In the top right corner, draw a small sun with five lines.

icebreakers.levelTip: Teaches shapes, sizes and position words.

icebreakers.name: Hidden Treasure Directions
steps: One team hides the treasure while the other waits outside.
The hiding team gives directions only in English.
The searching team follows step by step.
Swap roles.

confident: It's under something near the window.

icebreakers.levelTip: Count steps out loud for number practice.

icebreakers.name: Who Knows the Group?
materials: Questions written from students' earlier answers
steps: Earlier in the week, collect fun facts from students.
Turn them into quiz questions: 'Who has a pet turtle?'
Teams buzz in with a sound effect.
The person in the question says 'That's me!' and adds a detail.

confident: I remember ___ said something about that.

icebreakers.levelTip: Students love hearing their own facts in a quiz.

icebreakers.name: Longest Word Chain
steps: Each paper strip gets one English word.
Teams loop the strips into a chain.
Say every word out loud as you add it.
Longest chain wins. Hang them across the room.

confident: We can add ___ and ___ too.

icebreakers.levelTip: Leave the chains up all week as a word wall.

icebreakers.name: Talk Me Through
steps: Spread paper obstacles on the floor.
One partner walks with eyes closed. The other guides with words only and stays close.
Step on paper? Start again.
Switch roles. Anyone can keep their eyes open if they prefer.

confident: Careful, there's one just in front of your right foot.

icebreakers.levelTip: Partners walk next to each other for safety. Never force eyes closed.

icebreakers.name: Rhythm Names
steps: The group keeps a beat: clap, clap, snap, snap.
On the snaps, one person says their name and a food they love.
On the next snaps, the group repeats it.
Go around the circle without losing the beat.

confident: The name's ___, I'm crazy about ___!

icebreakers.levelTip: The rhythm helps students remember sentences and names.

icebreakers.name: Lost in the City
steps: Tape a city grid on the floor with landmark signs.
Each team gets a destination card.
One teammate walks the city. The others give directions from the side.
Fastest correct arrival wins.

middle: The bank is next to the park.
confident: Go past the school and take the second right.

icebreakers.levelTip: Uses the same places as Riding the bus and Opening a bank account.

icebreakers.name: Group Juggle
steps: Stand in a circle. Toss one ball across the circle, saying the catcher's name.
Keep the same order each round.
Add a second and third ball.
Then switch: say a word from a category instead of a name.

confident: Heads up, ___, coming your way!

icebreakers.levelTip: Chaos builds teamwork. Start slow.

icebreakers.name: Thank-You Circle
steps: Sit in a circle.
Each person says one thing they're thankful for today.
It can be big or small: a friend, lunch, the sun.
Others can say 'Me too' with a thumbs up.

confident: Something I don't say enough: thank you for ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: A calm way to end a busy day.

icebreakers.name: One-Word Weather
steps: Ask: 'If your mood was weather, what would it be?'
Each person says one weather word.
Sunny, cloudy, stormy, rainbow…
Anyone can add a sentence if they want.

confident: A bit stormy this morning, but sunnier now.

icebreakers.levelTip: Quick check-in that doesn't make anyone explain too much.

icebreakers.name: Silent Gallery Walk
steps: Hang students' work around the room.
Walk around quietly, like a museum.
Leave a kind sticky note on each piece.
Each artist reads their notes out loud to a partner.

middle: I like the ___ in your picture.
confident: Your drawing makes me feel ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Pair with Flag of Me or Three-Panel Me.

icebreakers.name: Breathe and Count
steps: Breathe in for four counts, out for four counts.
Count out loud in English.
Next round, a student counts in their home language.
Finish with one quiet breath together.

confident: Let's take one more slow breath.

icebreakers.levelTip: Use after a loud game or before a hard topic.

icebreakers.name: Letter to Future Me
steps: Write a short letter to yourself one year from now.
What do you hope will be different? What English will you know?
Seal it in an envelope.
Share one sentence out loud if you want.

middle: I hope I can ___ by next summer.
confident: Dear future me, I hope you've ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Keep the letters and give them back at the end of camp.

icebreakers.name: Compliment Chain
steps: Sit in a circle.
Give the person on your left a kind compliment.
They say thank you, then compliment the next person.
Go all the way around.

confident: Something I admire about you is ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Model specific compliments: 'You helped me today.'

icebreakers.name: Picture Story Starter
steps: Show a photo of a busy scene: a market, a bus, a park.
Everyone looks quietly for one minute.
Write or say three sentences about it.
Share the most creative sentence.

middle: A man is ___. A girl is ___.
confident: I think the woman is waiting for ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Beginners can point and name. Confident speakers invent a story.

icebreakers.name: Sentence Starter Jar
materials: A jar with sentence starters on paper
steps: Pass the jar around the circle.
Pull a starter: 'Something that makes me laugh is…'
Finish the sentence out loud.
Pass the jar on. You can swap once.

confident: One thing people don't know about me is ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Write easier starters on yellow paper, harder on blue.

icebreakers.name: Something From Home
materials: Students bring an object or a photo on their phone
steps: Ask students the day before to bring something that reminds them of home.
Sit in a circle.
Each person shows their object and says what it is.
Others can ask one gentle question.

confident: My ___ gave me this when ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Make sharing optional. Some memories are hard.

icebreakers.name: Listen and Draw
steps: Read a short scene slowly: 'There is a house. A tree is next to the house…'
Everyone draws what they hear.
Compare drawings.
A student describes the next scene.

middle: There is a cat under the tree.
confident: Behind the house, there's a small river.

icebreakers.levelTip: Pure listening practice. Calm and focused.

icebreakers.name: English Sign Hunt
steps: Walk around the building or outside.
Find English words on signs, posters and labels.
Write or photo three words you don't know.
Back together: share them and figure out what they mean.

middle: I saw the word ___ on a sign.
confident: I think ___ means ___ because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Shows students English is everywhere around them.

icebreakers.name: Two-Minute Journal
steps: Set a timer for two minutes.
Write or draw anything about your day.
When the timer ends, share one sentence with a partner.
Partners ask one question.

confident: Something I keep thinking about is ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Drawing counts. Any language in the journal is OK; share in English.

icebreakers.name: Sound Map
steps: Sit quietly for one minute with eyes closed.
Listen for every sound around you.
Draw a little map: put yourself in the middle and the sounds around you.
Share the sounds you heard.

confident: I could hear ___ coming from the hallway.

icebreakers.levelTip: Good reset when the group is too loud.

icebreakers.name: My English Goal
steps: Each person thinks of one thing they want to do in English this week.
Order food? Ask for help at school?
Write or draw it on a card.
Check the cards on Friday together.

middle: This week, I will ___ in English.
confident: My goal is to ___ without help.

icebreakers.levelTip: Celebrate every goal reached on Friday.

icebreakers.name: Favorite Word Collection
steps: Each person shares their favorite English word they learned this week.
Say why it's their favorite: the sound, the meaning, it's funny.
Add it to the word jar poster.
Teach the group your favorite word in your home language too.

confident: ___ is my favorite because it's so useful when ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: The poster grows all summer and shows how much they've learned.
